properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: reflow2 uses exactly TWO functions from dynograph-vector — mean and linear_regression_slope, both in dimensions.rs. The depth axis records DimensionObservations and computes drift as a slope WITHIN one dimension over time.

THE IDEA: pearson_correlation and spearman_rank_correlation (unused) would answer a question the axis cannot currently ask — do two dimensions move TOGETHER across components? "Does complexity track defect count?" "Does coupling track change frequency?" Spearman is the rank version, so it survives non-linear but monotone relationships and is the safer default on small samples.

CHEAP: pure functions, already a dependency, and the observations are already stored.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, and there are two. First, this is the most SPECULATIVE idea in the batch — no backlog item asks for it and no trial has reported wanting it, so it is a capability looking for a user. Second and more serious: correlation invites causal reading, and a design brain reporting "complexity correlates with defects" will be read as "complexity causes defects". The schema already takes this seriously — the CAUSES edge carries a `basis` enum (observed / correlational / causal / spurious) with the instruction "do not assert causal without a mechanism" — so the vocabulary for the caveat exists, but the report would have to carry it loudly.
properties.name: OPEN — should the depth axis compute CORRELATION between dimensions, not just drift within one?
properties.rationale: The only genuinely unexplored idea in dynograph-vector; the rest of that crate is either already used (mean, slope), already a parked question (embeddings), or thin (softmax, percentile).
